However, at the present time there has been no determination or intrepretation made by HEW on the issue of whether or not federally owned or trust minerals, when not held in conjunction with surface rights, constitute any eligibility for such an impact assistance program. If it were determined that mineral rights alone constitute eligibility it could mean a considerably larger advantage than eligibility based on surface ownership alone.
No other definitive educational assistance programs have been proposed although the State of Montana now requires a separate educational impact statement on any coal development. This presumably is to assist the school districts severely impacted by coal development in making their necessary adjustment and expansion.
Additional Law and Order - requirements can be mitigated by the tribe, county, and municipalities taking advantage of law enforcement assistance discretionary grants under the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 (as amended). This program provides funds for expanding law and order programs and the purchase of appropriate equipment. Technical assistance in the form of training can be provided under the technical assistance provisions of the act.
The Severe Housing Shortage - which is expected to result if a high degree of coal development is achieved rapidly, can be mitigated by a number of available programs. Their effectiveness, however, will be largely dependent on the entrepreneurship that is exercised by local housing developers. The motivation of these developers and the quality of the resulting housing development will be directly dependent on the effectiveness of the land use planning and enforcement programs.
